business_scope.primary_industry_name: Product Interface Design and Digital Design Subscription Agency

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: OECD Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (as extended to Gibraltar)
United Nations Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York Convention, extended via the United Kingdom)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar), as amended; Financial Services (Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing) Act 2018; Beneficial Ownership (Limited Partnerships) Regulations 2020, issued under the Beneficial Ownership Act 2019; Limited Partnerships Act 1993 (Gibraltar); Criminal Justice (International Co-operation) Act 2005; and the Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2020. These provisions incorporate international standards consistent with FATF Recommendation 24 and the EU 5th Anti-Money Laundering Directive framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized copy of UBO's valid passport (or national identity card for EEA/UK citizens)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of origin or residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address for each UBO and general partner (utility bill, bank statement or government-issued tax notice, dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, regulated financial institution or local government authority; signature notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the country of issue is not a party to the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or registration certificate for each corporate general partner or limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent authority of the corporate partner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter from a regulated financial institution for the partnership's primary funders and all UBOs, including source-of-wealth confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issue bank or credit institution licensed in the corresponding jurisdiction; signature notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Gibraltar registered agent / ELP general partner representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: UBOs and partners before a notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, limited partners, directors, and nominated beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, HM Treasury UK Financial Sanctions List, Gibraltar Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List (where applicable), OFAC SDN List, and the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit PEP database. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any match or PEP status is identified, requiring senior management approval descaling and source-of-wealth verification. Transaction and relationship monitoring is continuous and risk-based, with annual re-screening required for low-risk Design-As-A-Service entities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry online name reservation portal (Companies House Gibraltar) at https://www.companieshouse.gi
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name must be in the English language and Latin script. Only the 26 unaccented Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and the characters & - / , . ' are accepted. The name of an Exempted Limited Partnership must end with the suffix 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'L.P.'. Names must not create a false impression of being a body corporate, a bank, an insurer, a trust or a public authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the registered agent or applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, pursuant to section 46A of the Companies Act 2014 and the Limited Partnerships Act 1993. The appeal must include the name search results, any letters of non-objection from the relevant flag-protecting ministry or regulator where a sensitive token is involved, and a legal memorandum addressing the registry's stated objection. The Registrar must determine the appeal within 14 working days. If the rejection is upheld, a further appeal by way of statutory review lies to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar, which must be filed within 28 days. A reserved name may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon submission of a formal extension application and payment of the prescribed fee, provided the extension is not solely to avoid the expiry deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally permissible for administrative correspondence only. The Exempted Limited Partnership must maintain a physical registered office within Gibraltar at which official documents and legal process can be served. The registered office may be offered by a licensed company manager or registered agent; a purely virtual address without a substantive physical presence, clerical staff and access to records will not satisfy section 11 of the Limited Partnerships Act 1993. For the ISIC 7410 Design-As-A-Service subscription model, which is classified as Low_Risk_Standard, virtual office acceptance is typically available subject to the registered agent maintaining full physical substance arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspections by the Gibraltar Companies Registry, the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit or the Income Tax Office occur on a risk-based but moderate-low annual probability of approximately 10–15% for a low-risk Design-As-A-Service ELP. The likelihood increases if the partnership exhibits indicators of artificiality, including absence of locally maintained accounting records, lack of real decision-making in Gibraltar, or unexplained nominee arrangements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Companies (Fees) Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register initial filing and maintenance fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Beneficial Ownership (Fees) Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk Design-As-A-Service ELP with one UBO and two partners

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for tailored financial due diligence supporting payment institution onboarding

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act 2017 (Gibraltar), Part II (Registration of Limited Partnerships) and Part IV (Exempted Limited Partnerships); as supplemented by the Limited Partnerships (Amendment) Act 2019 and the Companies Act 2014 (registered office and registered agent obligations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 — Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Statement of Limited Partnership).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None — Gibraltar law imposes no minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for an Exempted Limited Partnership; capital contributions are determined contractually under the Limited Partnership Agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner hereby approves the registration of the Exempted Limited Partnership pursuant to the Limited Partnerships Act 2017 (Gibraltar) and the adoption of the Limited Partnership Agreement as initialed by the partners. RESOLVED, that the registered office be located at the offices of the registered agent in Gibraltar, as stated in the Statement of Limited Partnership. RESOLVED, that the initial partner be appointed as General Partner, with full authority to manage, bind, and represent the Partnership, and that the subscribing Limited Partners be admitted per the capital contribution schedule. RESOLVED, that the General Partner be authorized to open corporate bank and EMI accounts and to execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search and Availability Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar (online name search portal, HM Government of Gibraltar).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name availability inquiry via the Companies House search index; confirm the proposed ELP name contains no prohibited words and does not conflict with existing registered names or trademarks in Gibraltar; if the desired name is unavailable, submit rank-ordered alternative names. Names requiring consent (e.g., bank, trust) are excluded for this non-regulated digital design activity.
required_dossiers: Proposed entity name and alternative names
Name search request form
Identity and nationality details of the proposed General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, amend the proposed name and resubmit; no statutory fee is forfeited for name refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent / legal counsel in Gibraltar (private professional, not a state body).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Gibraltar-licensed professional to draft the Limited Partnership Agreement, including capital commitments, profit-sharing ratios, General Partner veto rights, Limited Partner non-participation language required by the Limited Partnerships Act 2017, registered office clause, exempted status clause, and dissolution mechanics. The agreement is executed by all partners in counterpart.
required_dossiers: Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Passport copies of all general and limited partners
Proof of residential/registered address of each partner
AML/KYC questionnaire and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar later queries a clause, file a supplementary deed of variation signed by all partners before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Form LP1 (Statement of Limited Partnership)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form LP1 together with the executed Limited Partnership Agreement and the prescribed filing fee. The form states the firm name, registered office in Gibraltar, nature of business (ISIC 7410 digital design services), registered agent details, and particulars of each partner. The General Partner must sign the declaration of compliance.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form LP1
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Consent of registered agent to act
Notice of registered office address in Gibraltar
Prescribed filing fee payable to the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of refusal or query, respond in writing within 21 days; amend and refile the defective form; a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Exempted Limited Partnership Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar (exempted status designation).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written application requesting designation as an Exempted Limited Partnership under Part IV of the Limited Partnerships Act 2017, declaring that the partnership is formed for design subscription services and, where relying on exempt status, will carry on business wholly or mainly outside Gibraltar; obtain the certificate of exempted status to evidence the pass-through classification.
required_dossiers: Application letter for exempted status
Certificate of registration (Form LP1 acknowledgement)
Declaration of intended business activities
Schedule of partner contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If exempted status is refused, submit fresh evidence of the partnership's overseas trade or non-resident ownership; request reconsideration by the Registrar within 28 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the Gibraltar Income Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ELP for Gibraltar income tax purposes to obtain a partnership tax reference and nil-liability notices for non-resident partners; as a pass-through entity the ELP itself is not taxed, but the General Partner must file annual partnership returns. If staff are hired, register for payroll withholdings with the same office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration and exempted status certificate
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Identities and residency status of all partners
Partnership tax registration form
Details of any Gibraltar-resident general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, provide the Income Tax Office with a certified copy of the Registrar's confirmation and attend the office for same-day administrative correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking and Payment-Rails Onboarding (Stripe Billing and Wise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (AML supervision); commercial bank or licensed EMI as contractual counterparty.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the certified registration pack to a Gibraltar-licensed bank or EMI (Wise) and to Stripe Billing for merchant underwriting; execute the First Resolution of the General Partner authorizing account opening; provide beneficial ownership declarations under the Gibraltar AML regime; complete SWIFT/SEPA instructions for B2B subscription invoicing.
required_dossiers: Certified certificate of registration and exempted status certificate
General Partner resolution authorizing bank/EMI accounts
Register of beneficial owners (AML filing)
Business plan and projected subscription revenue
Passport copies and proof of address of signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the institution requests enhanced due diligence, furnish a notarized source-of-funds statement and financial projections; contest unjustified refusal through the GFSC complaints process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing licence is mandated in Gibraltar for ISIC 7410 specialized design services; the activity is categorised as a professional service.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required (no manufacturing or operating permit); optional but recommended: data protection registration with the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority under the Data Protection Act 2004 (GDPR regime) for processing client data in the course of design subscription services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, HM Government of Gibraltar.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical installation; serviced-office operations do not trigger an Environmental Impact Assessment under the Gibraltar Town Planning/EIA regulations (Category C, non-scheduled activity).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero industrial wastewater or VOC discharge; office waste handled through municipal collection under the Waste Management Regulations; IT hardware disposed in compliance with WEEE obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate to be obtained under the Fire Safety (Gibraltar) legislation for the registered office premises; Building Control occupancy load and emergency-exit inspection through the Property and Building Control Office; workplace health and safety compliance under the Health and Safety at Work (Gibraltar) Act, including first-aid provision and electrical equipment certification for desk-based operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar; official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An Exempted Limited Partnership is registered with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies and must complete a tax registration application to the Income Tax Office. The application is submitted by the registered agent or a licensed local representative, accompanied by the ELP certificate of registration, a certified copy of the partnership agreement, and identification details of all partners. The Income Tax Office then issues a Gibraltar TIN. Where an overseas partnership seeks to carry on activity in Gibraltar, an ordinary non-resident partnership registration form must be filed, and the Commissioner determines whether the partnership is fiscally transparent or assessable in accordance with the Income Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no check-the-box election. The ELP is fiscally transparent by default; profits and losses flow through to partners. No statutory election is available to convert an ELP into an entity taxed as a company for Gibraltar tax purposes solely by shareholder choice. Hybrid mismatch rules (based on the EU ATAD framework) apply to payments and structures involving hybrid entities, with mechanisms to deny deductions or impose corresponding adjustments where there is double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar does not operate a VAT, GST, or general sales and use tax; indirect taxation is limited to customs import duties, excise duties on specific goods, and stamp duty on particular transactions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable. There is no VAT/GST registration threshold in Gibraltar. Businesses supplying digital services are not required to register for any Gibraltar indirect tax. Importers of goods subject to customs or excise duties must register with Her Majesty's Customs Gibraltar for each importation; this obligation arises from the first import rather than at a turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or government clearance platform is in force for Gibraltar invoices. B2B invoices may be issued electronically by mutual agreement. Records must be retained for tax audit purposes, but there is no digital fiscal authentication requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Because Gibraltar does not levy VAT, exported goods and digital UI/UX design subscription services are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax rather than zero-rated. For any physical goods element, the exporter must demonstrate that the goods were physically exported from Gibraltar and delivered outside Gibraltar. For digital services, the eligibility condition is that the supplier is established in Gibraltar, the customer is a non-Gibraltar resident, and the place of supply is outside Gibraltar. No prior tax authority approval or licence is required for intangible design services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration (Geneva/SAD equivalent) — required only when physical goods cross the frontier
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Gibraltar and arrival abroad
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit confirmation showing cross-border payment receipt from an overseas customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported export exemption claims may trigger retrospective clawback of any duty relief granted, addition of interest from the original duty point, and penalties of up to 100% of the duty evaded. Criminal sanctions apply under Gibraltar's Customs and Excise Duties Act for knowingly making false declarations. Partners of the ELP may be held jointly and severally liable for any penalty attributable to false indirect-tax export claims, and the ELP's records and bank accounts may be the subject of tax authority inspection and restraint orders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority) and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as banking regulator and AML supervisor
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Capital and current account transactions are fully liberalised. The Gibraltar pound is pegged at par to GBP; there are no Gibraltar exchange controls and no restrictions on currency convertibility. Profit remittance, distribution, and capital repatriation may be made freely in GBP or any convertible currency, subject only to GFSC AML record-keeping and suspicious transaction reporting requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation, no conversion timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio apply to export receipts. Foreign currency export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in any convertible denomination. Only standard corporate record-keeping, tax documentation, and AML/CFT reporting thresholds govern cross-border receipt movements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Regulated European Economic Area or UK EMI authorisations do not automatically passport to Gibraltar. Offshore digital EMIs may onboard a Gibraltar exempted limited partnership only where their internal country-approval matrix expressly covers British Overseas Territories. Feasibility is therefore conditional on EMI risk appetite, underlying clearing bank, and GFSC-licensed sponsor relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for physical appearance at a Gibraltar bank for an ELP. Remote onboarding is permissible with high-definition video verification, digitally certified passport copies, and independent source-of-funds evidence. Certain banks require a personal interview of at least one general partner or senior controller, conducted remotely or at the bank’s Gibraltar premises via a regulated introducer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed ultimate beneficial ownership of the limited partnership due to pass-through structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed deed of partnership; full entitlement schedule; CFPs/UCIS certificates; GFSC-compliant UBO register; explanation of general partner control; certified constitutional documents of all underlying owners

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident owners residing in or holding citizenship of high-risk third countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth statement supported by bank statements and title or sale deeds; independent sanctions and adverse-media screening report; audited or accountant-certified financials; tax residence certificates; explanation of business nexus to Gibraltar

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Design-as-a-service subscription model with low physical substance and recurring digital cross-border revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client subscription agreements; invoices and payment settlement records; subcontractor and contributor agreements; website/platform terms of service; evidence of genuine administrative and management oversight from Gibraltar; transfer-pricing documentation if applicable

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound capital injection from cross-border venture or lender without pre-existing commercial relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution resolution; financing or investment term sheet; bank statement from originating institution; beneficial-owner debt-to-equity schedule; confirmation that funds are not derived from digital-asset mixing or unregulated financial services; AML questionnaire completed by source institution

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is routed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with purpose code CAPT or CRCP for capital and reserve contributions. SEPA Credit Transfer is preferred for EUR-denominated injections; GBP injections use Faster Payments or CHAPS. The payment message must identify the ELP, the GFSC registration or incorporation number, and the reference matching the signed capital contribution form. Beneficiary bank is mandated to verify the UBO schedule before crediting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements and operating disbursements are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic payments, Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) for purchase-order-based transactions, SEPA Direct Debit for recurring EU Euler/euro obligations, and Faster Payments or CHAPS for United Kingdom supplier invoices. Inbound subscription card receipts from Stripe settle in GBP to the Gibraltar operational account; bulk contractor payouts are made through Wise’s licensed rails using local clearing such as ACH, SEPA, and UK FPS, depending on beneficiary currency and jurisdiction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla Currency Options executed through a GFSC-regulated or equivalent authorised broker

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of Exempted Limited Partnership and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Companies House Gibraltar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the effective registration date of the partnership; the first annual return may cover a period exceeding 12 months if the registration date is more than 12 months before the first return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing penalty of approximately GBP 60 per month accrues, subject to a cap of GBP 600; continued non-filing for three consecutive years permits the Registrar to commence administrative strike-off and dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Exempted Limited Partnership Economic Substance Return (ESR Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office through the Registrar of Companies (Single Submissions Portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For partnerships with a calendar financial year, filing is required by 31 December of the immediately following calendar year; for non-calendar financial years, filing is required within 12 months of the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Written non-compliance notice from the Commissioner of Income Tax; financial penalties up to GBP 50,000 per year of non-compliance; recurrent non-compliance may result in the loss of tax-exempt status designation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Exempted Limited Partnership is not subject to a mandatory independent audit solely by reason of its legal form. A statutory audit becomes compulsory if the partnership is required by its partnership deed or by applicable law to present certified accounts and the partnership exceeds either an annual turnover of GBP 1,000,000 or a balance-sheet total of GBP 2,000,000; a qualifying audit exemption may apply if the partnership is not a collective investment scheme and all partners have consented to an exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted for use in Gibraltar (EU-adopted IFRS) applies for statutory transparency; small entities may elect to apply Gibraltar-adopted FRS 102 (UK GAAP) as the accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners and limited partners. Any transfer of partnership interest must be recorded in the register and, where the underlying ownership changes are reportable, filed with the Registrar within 28 days of the transfer. The annual return submitted to Companies House Gibraltar includes an annual confirmation that the beneficial ownership information is complete and current, with each general partner certifying the accuracy.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 1,200 per annum for registered office maintenance, registered agent services, and statutory filing administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – USD 6,000 per annum for a certified Gibraltar audit engagement; USD 700 – USD 1,500 for a relevant accounts compilation/review where a statutory audit is expressly exempted

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat corporate rate under the Income Tax Act 2010 (as amended). The Gibraltar Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) is fiscally transparent: no tax is imposed at the partnership level; each partner is assessed on their allocable share.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar is within the charge. For an ELP whose UI/UX design subscription revenue is derived exclusively from non-Gibraltar clients and whose operations are managed outside Gibraltar, the effective Gibraltar tax rate on non-resident partners is 0%. No capital gains tax, no VAT/GST, no wealth tax, no inheritance tax on non-resident partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (trading losses may be carried forward indefinitely and set off against future profits of the same trade; no statutory time limitation)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Partnership Income Tax Information Return (ELP pass-through return) filed via the Gibraltar Income Tax Office (GITO) e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the ELP's chargeable period (accounting year-end). Where accounts coincide with the statutory Year of Assessment (1 July - 30 June), the filing deadline is 31 December following the year of assessment unless an extension is granted by the Commissioner of Income Tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ELP registration details: name, ELP registration number, registered office in Gibraltar, general partner (GP) identity and principal place of business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm non-resident status of each partner and provide the partners' country of tax residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of accounting profits and losses between the general partner and each limited partner in accordance with the ELP agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify each partner's share of Gibraltar-source income separately from non-Gibraltar-source income; only the Gibraltar-source share is assessable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gibraltar-source gross receipts: subscription fees, design licensing revenue, and service fees attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners with no Gibraltar PE and no Gibraltar-source income should enter nil here; attach a supporting statement of territoriality.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: salaries, software subscriptions, cloud infrastructure, subcontractor design costs, and regulatory levies incurred in producing assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in deriving Gibraltar-source income are deductible against the assessable share; allocation must be auditable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and withholding accounts (if any), including foreign tax credits available under the UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should not claim Gibraltar credits for foreign taxes unless such taxes are attributable to Gibraltar-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration: signature by the general partner (or an authorised director of the corporate GP), confirming the return is complete and accurate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The corporate GP signs under penalty of perjury; knowing false declarations expose the GP and its directors to personal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of GBP 100 plus daily default penalty (typically GBP 10/day up to 90 days); continued failure after six months attracts a further tax-geared penalty up to 100% of the chargeable tax. Interest accrues on unpaid tax at the statutory rate from the due date. Deliberate or reckless inaccuracy may be prosecuted as tax evasion (imprisonment up to seven years).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Gibraltar imposes no withholding tax on dividends, profit distributions, or partnership allocations to partners, whether resident or non-resident).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Gibraltar does not levy dividend/interest/royalty withholding tax, no treaty relief or reclaim procedure is required for outbound payments. Where a partner is UK-resident and seeks to evidence that UK tax should not be applied on a Gibraltar-source flow, the partner may apply to the Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax for a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC); the TRC application requires statutory declarations, financial statements, and substance evidence. Relief is then accessed under the UK-Gibraltar DTA (signed 2019) through HMRC's procedures. No refund mechanism exists within Gibraltar for tax not withheld at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% on cross-border royalties (including UI/UX design IP licensing) and 0% on debt interest paid by a Gibraltar entity to non-residents. Under the UK-Gibraltar DTA, no source-state withholding applies to royalties or interest; the amounts remain taxable only in the beneficial owner's state of residence, subject to the DTA's limitation of benefits and anti-abuse clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country Report and Master File: MNE groups with consolidated group revenue equal to or exceeding EUR 750 million (reported to the GITO). Local File: required where the Gibraltar entity's controlled transactions exceed GBP 1 million in aggregate per accounting period; for the ELP, intercompany charges to/from UK affiliates must be contemporaneously documented. Lower thresholds apply where the Commissioner directs on risk-based grounds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to all Gibraltar tax-resident entities and partnerships, including ELPs. UI/UX design subscription services constitute a 'distribution and service centre' relevant activity. The ELP must maintain in Gibraltar: (i) physical premises, (ii) local qualified staff proportionate to the scale of activity, (iii) operating expenditure, and (iv) board/management governance in Gibraltar. A 'pure equity holding' exemption is unavailable because the ELP carries an active service trade. Non-compliance attracts civil penalties up to GBP 100,000 per financial period, correction directions, strike-off, and the denial of a tax residence certificate (with consequential DTA exposure).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false or incomplete partnership return; omitting Gibraltar-source subscription income; inflating deductible expenses; using nominee arrangements to conceal the true general partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty up to 100% of the tax undercharged plus daily interest; criminal prosecution before the Supreme Court of Gibraltar; fine and/or imprisonment for up to seven years; confiscation orders for proceeds of the evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are personally liable for fraudulent trading and are subject to civil restitution orders, statutory disqualification, departure prohibition orders preventing them from leaving Gibraltar until tax is secured, and imprisonment in cases of deliberate concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the ELP's Gibraltar registration without physical premises, personnel, or expenditure in Gibraltar; outsourcing all design operations to non-resident subcontractors while claiming Gibraltar tax residence for DTA benefits; submitting false ESR substance declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty up to GBP 100,000 per relevant financial period; penalty for material false statement (fine and imprisonment up to two years); mandated correction direction requiring substance to be established within a fixed window; strike-off from the Gibraltar Register of Limited Partnerships; denial of tax residence status; adverse exchange-of-information findings under the OECD Forum on Harmful Tax Practices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate GP face personal liability for the ESR penalty where the partnership was used as a vehicle to obtain an improper tax advantage; the Supreme Court may issue a travel ban and add penalties on the GP's assets; directors may be disqualified under the Companies Act for up to 15 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing client subscription payments through Stripe and Wise without a Gibraltar AML risk assessment, without customer due diligence on UK/EU subscribers, or failing to file a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) where subscription proceeds are suspected to represent third-party funds or sanctions-evasion proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering: conviction on indictment carries imprisonment up to 14 years and an unlimited fine; failure to disclose suspicious activity: imprisonment up to five years and a fine; tipping-off offences carry imprisonment up to two years; civil penalties may be imposed by the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate GP are treated as senior management and can be individually prosecuted for consenting to or conniving in the offence; personal confiscation orders, travel bans, and disqualification orders may be imposed; the corporate veil is pierced where the ELP is used as the laundering vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Managing the design subscription business from the UK (key decisions, staff, and client negotiation conducted in London) while booking all profit to the Gibraltar ELP, without the ELP charging an arm's-length service fee or the UK branch retaining a taxable profit share; structuring solely to exploit the 0% effective rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reallocation of profits to a UK permanent establishment under UK corporate tax rules; UK corporation tax at up to 25% on attributable profits; application of UK GAAR (penalty up to 100% of the counteracted tax advantage); Gibraltar GAAR and transfer pricing adjustments with world-wide allocation of profits, plus interest and penalties up to 100% of the additional assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate GP are personally involved if they knowingly signed returns reflecting the abusive structure; UK and Gibraltar authorities may issue cross-border enquiry notices, travel bans, and, in cases of deliberate concealment, extradition-eligible criminal proceedings; personal civil liability for the partnership's unpaid tax arises where the GP is a façade with no independent assets.
